subject_group: 9.6.3 Emergency ground, ditching, and water egress

versions.text:
Standard: All crewmembers and passengers can egress from the air vehicle within the specified time using only half the exits under day and night lighting conditions. Rotary-wing exits and sizes have twice the capacity for the maximum number of occupants to egress in the specified time. The crewmember and passenger areas allow for complete abandonment in the specified time during ground egress or ditching of the air vehicle, with the landing gear extended as well as retracted, considering the possibility of the air vehicle being on fire, and at maximum seating capacity. For air vehicles with non-crashworthy fuel cells: All crewmembers can egress in 20 seconds using only one-half the exits. For air vehicles with crashworthy fuel cells: All crewmembers can egress in 30 seconds using only one-half the exits. For air vehicles that carry passengers: All crewmembers and passengers can egress in 60 seconds using only one-half the exits. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Review analysis that shows that that the equipped crewmember and passengers can egress the air vehicle from that combination of a selection of half the exits which results in the most restrictive configuration. Analysis includes crewmembers and passengers across the intended anthropometric range. Test.
  (1) Ground or Lab test: Testing verifies that the appropriately equipped (mission representative) crewmembers and passengers can egress the air vehicle from that combination of a random selection of half the exits which results in the most restrictive configuration. Tests include participants across the intended user anthropometric range. An emergency egress test from the air vehicle or a high-fidelity mockup is used to verify egress capability and time required under both day and night lighting conditions.
